title: Kernel Ridge Regression-Based Graph Dataset Distillation

problem.claim: Distill a given graph dataset while retaining most of the trained models' performance.

gap.claim: Existing meta-learning-based bilevel optimization methods require computationally intensive exact solutions and therefore rely on approximations that can hurt distillation performance.

contributions.claim: Adopt a kernel ridge regression-based meta-learning objective with a feasible exact solution.
Design LiteGNTK, a graph kernel tailored to graph dataset distillation and closely related to the random walk graph kernel.
Propose KIDD and its variants for kernel ridge regression-based graph dataset distillation.

author_reported_evidence.claim: KIDD shows efficiency in both forward and backward propagation.
KIDD shows strong empirical performance over 7 real-world datasets compared with state-of-the-art distillation methods.
KIDD can sometimes outperform the original whole training set using as few as 1.65% of the training graphs.

narrative_sequence.summary: Large graph datasets support strong GNN performance but make training computationally expensive.
Graph dataset distillation must preserve trained-model performance, while existing bilevel methods are expensive and approximation-dependent.
The paper uses a kernel ridge regression objective, introduces LiteGNTK, and proposes KIDD and its variants.
The authors report propagation efficiency, strong results across 7 real-world datasets, and occasional gains over the full training set at 1.65% of its size.

source_observation.claim: The method uses an objective with a feasible exact solution to address approximation-related performance loss.

interpretation.claim: Replacing an expensive approximate optimization procedure with an efficiently solvable exact formulation may improve both tractability and fidelity.

application.claim: When designing dataset compression methods, consider reformulating the objective around a solver-friendly model whose solution can be computed exactly.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that exact solvability consistently improves performance across all datasets or tasks.

source_observation.claim: The paper introduces a task-specific graph kernel to reduce the cost of computing the graph neural tangent kernel.

interpretation.claim: Task-specific approximations or substitutes can make theoretically useful representations practical when the original computation is too expensive.

application.claim: For computationally heavy kernel-based workflows, design a representation tailored to the target task and its bottleneck.

exception.claim: The abstract does not quantify the computational savings or characterize when LiteGNTK preserves the relevant properties of the graph neural tangent kernel.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the 7 datasets, evaluation metrics, or baseline results.
The abstract does not describe the exact KIDD objective, optimization procedure, or kernel construction.
The abstract does not provide independent verification or reproducibility details.
